52.51431,0.67969: 'Allo 'Allo! 1982-1992 by Jeremy Lloyd OBE and David Croft OBE filmed here
52.57108,0.82758: The Old Police Station Built in 1855 at a cost of £950. It has cells for the temporary confinement of the accused and was manned by an Inspector, Sergeant and three Constables.
52.5712,0.82509: Crown Hotel Built c. 1760, during the 19th century the Crown Hotel was used for horse trading, had stabling for 200 horses and its own horse doctor.
52.5712,0.82726: The Willow House Built c. 1556, the Willow House is one of the oldest surviving houses in Watton and has been a vicarage, a school, a laundry and a dentists surgery.
52.57126,0.81862: This building believed to have been erected in 1819, became the National School
52.57139,0.82102: The Old Brewery Built in three stages by Edward Stevens and his son in 1831, 1838 and 1877. Production ceased in about 1912 after it had been taken over by Morgans Brewery of Norwich
52.57152,0.82529: The Clock Tower Built in 1679 by Christopher Hey a mercer of Watton. The lower part of the building was the town lock-up and it is believed that the top held a bell to warn of fire.
52.64812,0.68814: The Cornhall. Built in 1858, in the Italianate style. Corn was sold here on market days, but it was used for social gatherings and entertainment at other times.
52.65888,0.52594: Constance Baker née Ketteringham 'Mother of the Wounded' attended school here Born 21 June 1868 - Marham Died 28 August 1929
52.66798,0.96375: George Borrow the novelist was born here 1803
52.68085,0.93813: The Bell Tower. This unusual 16th Century structure was necessary because the Church tower was not strong enough to hold the bells. John de Narde, a French prisoner from the Napoleonic War, escaped from the building. He was later shot and lies buried in the churchyard.
52.68092,0.93917: The Romany Rye. These licensed premises were purpose-built as a hotel, in 1965, and are named after the novel by George Borrow, who was born on the outskirts of East Dereham, in 1803. 'One of the most imaginative prose writers of the 19th century', his world-wide travels provided the inspiration for his best boooks such as Romany Rye, written in 1857. These premises were refurbished by J D Wetherspoon and re-opened in April 2011.
52.68251,0.94109: From 1766 to 1794 the home of Sir John Fenn 1739-1794 Scholar & Antiquary He discovered and here transcribed the famous 15th Century Paston Letters
52.68251,0.9411: From 1766 to 1813 the home of Lady Ellenor Fenn 1743-1813 Pioneering educationalist & writer for children under the names Mrs Lovechild & Mrs Techwell Her most notable publication was "Cobwebs to Catch Flies"
52.90925,0.75608: Near this place at 11.00pm on 27th April 1944, Mosquito Fighter Bomber MK VI Serial LR329 305 Squadron R.A.F crashed whilst on a night training exercise. The crew, Flying Officer (Pilot) John Edward Mathias D.F.C aged 23 and Flight Lt (Navigator) Thomas Wilson Irwin aged 23, were killed. May they rest in peace.
52.9203,0.94916: JACK'S GATE Erected by Friends of Binham Priory in memory of Honorary Member John Ernest (Jack) Grange 1930-2014 life-long resident of Binham and staunch supporter of Binham Priory April 2015
52.92976,0.76028: The Birthplace of Admiral Lord Nelson The Old Rectory in which the Admiral was born stood twenty yards back from this wall. It was pulled down in 1803
